cards.name: Shell Lower
cards.summary: Warp style that keeps the top edge straight at its original width while the sides sweep outward in concave curves to two points a little below the middle, and the bottom edge bows down into a wide convex arc between them: a bell, lampshade or skirt silhouette. Strong at the 50% default: in the harvest render a 300 x 200 rectangle grew to about 580 px at its widest and about 260 px tall.
use_for: retro / varsity badge type whose baseline curves down under a flat cap line
bottom line of a crest, seal or sports logo
skirt or bell-shaped banner from a plain rectangle
vintage poster headline with a flared base
avoid: art that must keep its footprint: it nearly doubles the width at 50% Bend, so leave room or scale the result down; Arc Lower gives a gentler curve on the bottom only
small body text: the flared ends stretch letters badly; keep it to short headlines
if the top should flare instead, use Shell Upper

params.name: DeformStyle
params.does: which Warp style the Adobe Deform effect draws; this item stores 6 = Shell Lower. Another value turns the effect into a different Warp style (Arc, Flag, Fisheye ...)

params.name: DeformValue
params.does: Bend: how far the bottom flares and bows down (fraction, 0.5 = 50%); a negative value turns the curve the other way

params.name: DeformHoriz
params.does: Horizontal Distortion: tapers the warped art left-to-right like a perspective squeeze (fraction, 0.2 = 20%)

params.name: DeformVert
params.does: Vertical Distortion: tapers the warped art top-to-bottom (fraction, 0.2 = 20%)

params.name: Rotate
params.does: the Horizontal / Vertical orientation choice of Warp Options; true = Vertical, which runs the warp along the other axis

pairs_with: Shell Upper on a line of type set above it, for a two-line crest
Effect > Stylize > Drop Shadow after the warp for a sticker look
Object > Expand Appearance before sending to a cutter or another app
cards.scripting: item.applyEffect('<LiveEffect name="Adobe Deform"><Dict data="I DeformStyle 6 R DeformValue 0.5 R DeformHoriz 0.0 R DeformVert 0.0 B Rotate 0"/></LiveEffect>')  // menu route: select the object, app.executeMenuCommand("Live Deform Shell Lower") opens the Warp Options dialog (needs an OK). DisplayString (the Appearance label 'Warp: Shell Lower') was left out of the verified call: Dict values with spaces are not proven.
cards.non_destructive: yes: live effect listed as the Warp entry in the Appearance panel, editable by double-clicking it; Object > Expand Appearance bakes it into paths
cards.cost: low: vector live effect re-evaluated on every edit; noticeably slower on long type blocks or very complex groups

review.changes: summary: the render's widest point is a little below the middle, not 'across the bottom', and the shape also grows to ~260 px tall (measured on Effect_Warp_Shell_Lower.png)

verified.note: The top of the group stays at its height while the sides sweep outward toward the bottom (box and circle flare past the left and right edges) and the bottom bows down (the type grows and drops, the zigzag runs off the bottom), the strong bell / skirt flare the card describes at 50 %.

cards.name: Shell Upper
cards.summary: Warp style that keeps the bottom edge straight at its original width while the sides sweep outward in concave curves to two points a little above the middle, and the top edge rises into a wide convex arc between them: a fan or scallop-shell silhouette. In the harvest render a 300 x 200 rectangle at 50% Bend grew to about 580 px at its widest and about 260 px tall over the unchanged base.
use_for: arched vintage headline sitting on a flat baseline
top line of a team crest, badge or label
fan / shell shapes from rectangles and stripes
bakery, barber or diner style retro logos
avoid: layouts with no headroom: the arc and flare spread the art well beyond its box; Arc Upper bends only the top with less spread
long lines of type: the outer letters get stretched wide
if the base should flare instead, use Shell Lower

cards.name: Squeeze
cards.summary: Warp style that pinches the left and right sides inward into concave curves while the top and bottom edges bulge outward, so the art gets a pinched waist like a cushion squeezed from both sides. The corners stay roughly in place; at 50% Bend the harvest render rectangle's sides pulled in by about 12% each.
use_for: punchy compressed headline that looks squeezed in the middle
comic or sticker type with a pinched pillow shape
hourglass / bow-tie shaped frames and banners from rectangles
with Rotate (Vertical) for art pinched top and bottom instead
avoid: text that must stay readable at small sizes: every letter is pinched at mid-height and the end letters bend along the concave sides
if the middle should swell instead, use Effect > Warp > Inflate (sides bow out) or Warp > Bulge (top and bottom only), not the 3D Inflate effect
a negative Bend pushes the sides outward: check the sign before batch-applying

review.changes: avoid: 'centre letters get very narrow' contradicted the render (the pinch is on the left/right sides at mid-height; the centre bulges taller); named Warp > Inflate / Bulge explicitly since Effect/3D and Materials/Inflate also exists

verified.note: At Bend 0.7 the left and right ends are pinched inward with concave curves (the box's left side and the circle's right side curve in, the zigzag is pulled narrower) while the top and bottom bulge out (the star grows taller, the zigzag drops), the pinched-waist look the card describes.

cards.name: Twist
cards.summary: Warp style that twists the art around its centre so inner content turns relative to the edges, while the outer edges bend into S-curves. Weak on simple outlines: on a plain rectangle at 50% Bend the harvest render barely changed (edges moved about 2 px, mean pixel difference 0.67). On grouped art at full Bend (1.0) the turn is strong: on the test plate the star swirled into a pinwheel, the type turned and the box, circle and zigzag were swept into S-shapes.
use_for: playful dizzy or spinning headline type
adding a sense of motion to a logo mark or icon group
a subtle hand-made wobble on lettering when kept at low Bend
avoid: plain shapes with little inside them: the outline hardly moves, so nothing seems to happen
a real spiral or strong rotation: use Effect > Distort & Transform > Twist (angle-based) or the Twirl tool
body text: twisted letters lose legibility fast

review.changes: removed CDR Toolbox/Distort/Twister: it spins the outline into a spiral (its own card maps it to AI Effect/Distort & Transform/Twist, which this card's avoid list already sends spiral jobs to), while Warp Twist leaves the outline almost unchanged; dropped 'swirl' / 'pinwheel' from look and summary for the same reason (the render shows ~2 px edge movement)

verified.note: At Bend 1.0 the grouped art twists around its centre: the star swirls into a pinwheel, the type turns, and the box, circle and zigzag are swept into curved S-shapes, the twist the card describes; text corrected while passing: the frame answers the card's open question (at full Bend on grouped art the turn is strong, not subtle).

cards.name: Wave
cards.summary: Warp style that runs a wave across the width of the art so its content ripples up and down. On a plain rectangle the outline hardly moves (harvest render at 50% Bend: only a faint S on the top and bottom edges, mean pixel difference 0.42), so the ripple shows mainly in type and grouped shapes; a different look from Flag, which swings the whole outline into a big S.
use_for: wavy fun headline for kids, summer or beach posters
water, sound or music themed lettering
rippling stripes or patterns built from groups
avoid: single plain shapes: the outline barely changes; use Flag for a strong S-wave of the whole silhouette
even, repeating ripple edges: use Effect > Distort & Transform > Zig Zag with Smooth points
small text: rippled letters lose legibility
